name: Tool_Crafting_System
description: Building tools from raw materials: assembly at crafting stations, material properties affecting tool stats, upgrade paths, and creative tool combinations.

questions.question: Does crafting teach real materials engineering and tool design?
questions.answer: Yes. Tool stats depend on material properties: density, tensile strength, hardness, thermal conductivity. Player chooses head/handle/binding materials with real engineering tradeoffs.

questions.question: Does tool crafting generate shareable 'look what I made' content?
questions.answer: Yes. Material-property-driven crafting means every tool is unique. 'I built a tungsten-tipped drill with carbon-fiber handle' is shareable achievement content.

questions.question: Are crafting materials distributed realistically across the world?
questions.answer: Yes. Materials follow real geology: basalt in volcanic regions, hematite in iron deposits, chert in chalk formations. Player learns real geology by gathering.

questions.question: Can basic crafting be prototyped in one sprint?
questions.answer: Partially. Material-to-tool assembly with 3 material types (stone, iron, obsidian) and 2 tool schemas can be prototyped in 5-7 days. Uses existing UE5 inventory system.

questions.question: Is crafting system data-driven and extendable?
questions.answer: Yes. Material properties, craftable schemas, and station capabilities are DataTable-driven. Adding new materials or tools requires only data changes.

questions.question: Does crafting work in UE5.8 without hacks?
questions.answer: Yes. Inventory system, UMG crafting UI, data tables, Chaos Physics assembly -- all standard UE5.8. No engine modifications.

questions.question: Does crafting system impact performance on RTX 3060?
questions.answer: No. Crafting is UI-driven with negligible CPU cost (material lookup = memory read, assembly animation = one-time event). No ongoing impact.

questions.question: Can a colorblind or hearing-impaired player fully use crafting?
questions.answer: Yes. Material properties shown as text + icons, not color-only. High-contrast labels. Assembly feedback is visual (tool appears on bench) with optional audio.

questions.question: Does crafting have satisfying sound feedback?
questions.answer: v1: place material (thud/click), assemble (hammer + scrape), complete (confirmation chime). Each material has distinct handling sound (stone clink, metal ring).

questions.question: Does crafting work with multiple players?
questions.answer: v1 is single-player. Multiplayer features (shared stations, collaborative assembly, material pooling) are v2.

questions.question: Can community create custom tools and materials?
questions.answer: Yes. Material property tables, crafting schemas, and station definitions are all data-driven. Modders add entire new tool tiers and material families.

questions.question: Can crafting system be localized?
questions.answer: Yes. Material names, property labels, schema names, and station names use FText. Numerical stats are locale-formatted.

questions.question: Does Tool_Crafting_System depend on Scanner_Tool_Implementation?
questions.answer: Partially. Scanner identifies materials for crafting unlock. Basic crafting works with pre-scanned materials, but scan-to-craft is the designed flow.

questions.question: Does crafting prove that educational engineering can BE the gameplay?
questions.answer: Yes. Choosing materials by real engineering properties to create different-performing tools proves educational content IS the gameplay, not a layer on top.

questions.question: Was Tool_Crafting_System derived from Tool_Systems Q11 (upgrades) and Q4 (combinations)?
questions.answer: Yes. Tool_Systems Q11 answered 'Tools can be upgraded.' Q4 answered 'Tools can be combined.' This sub-feature materializes both as a unified crafting system.

questions.question: Does crafting conflict with the environmental demo focus?
questions.answer: Minor. Crafting asset creation takes time from environment art. Acceptable: crafting gives environmental resources a purpose in the core loop.

questions.question: What UE5 knowledge is required for crafting system?
questions.answer: Inventory system, UMG UI, data tables, Chaos Physics. Moderate-high difficulty. 1-2 weeks for core loop with 3 material types.

questions.question: Does this need sub-features?
questions.answer: Not at this level. Future sub-features: Tool_Material_Properties_Engine, Crafting_Station_Tiers, Tool_Upgrade_Paths.

questions.question: Are siblings missing at this level?
questions.answer: No. Scanner (discovery), Durability (lifecycle), Crafting (creation) form a complete tool system: discover materials -> craft tools -> use -> maintain.

questions.question: Is Tool_Systems complete enough for this?
questions.answer: Yes. Tool_Systems confirmed tool crafting, material-based stats, and upgrade paths at DESIGNED status.

questions.question: Should Tool_Crafting_System be built before or after siblings?
questions.answer: Build third, after scanner and durability. Crafting needs scanner (material ID) and produces tools needing durability. It is the capstone.

questions.question: What does crafting system block?
questions.answer: Blocks player tool-tier progression and the resource economy. Does not block scanner or durability.

questions.question: Does crafting system serve the educational RPG goal?
questions.answer: Yes. Crafting teaches materials engineering, tool design, geology (material sourcing), and resource logistics. Real engineering through making tools.

questions.question: What is sacrificed by building crafting now?
questions.answer: Crafting is the most complex of the three systems (assets, UI, data tables). Building it now defers other loop-4 tools. Acceptable: crafting is foundational.

questions.question: What evidence shows material-property crafting engages players?
questions.answer: Minecraft's wood/stone/iron/diamond tier progression and Subnautica's material-based tool crafting prove this pattern is deeply engaging in sci-fi settings.

questions.question: Does crafting chain reach a human learning real skills?
questions.answer: Yes. Player learns: material selection determines tool performance (engineering), rock cycle determines availability (geology), logistics requires planning (supply chain).
